Anthropic signed a six-year computing agreement worth $13.7 billion with Rum Group, a company with roots in social media and longstanding Trump-administration ties.

The Details:

•	Contract value: The agreement is worth $13.7 billion over six years, according to a person familiar with the matter.

•	Capacity total: Anthropic’s agreements total at least 14.8 gigawatts of compute capacity.

•	Aggregate cost: Those compute agreements could cost as much as $517 billion over the next decade.

FOMC decision week began with a clear AI rotation: long software, short semis. Nvidia $NVDA, Marvell $MRVL, Sandisk $SNDK, AMD $AMD, Nebius $NBIS, Micron $MU, CoreWeave $CRWV, and Intel $INTC were down 3%-7%, while Palantir $PLTR, Atlassian $TEAM, CrowdStrike $CRWD, ServiceNow $NOW, Adobe $ADBE, and Intuit $INTU were up 2%-5%. The move reflected a market trying to reprice the AI trade after the weekend’s safety debate around Dario’s essay. Semis and neoclouds sold off because their bull case is tied directly to continued AI capex growth which the market interpreted as slowing down if the pace of frontier model development slows down. The Clarity Act $BTC $ETH failed to advance in the Senate on Sept. 15, with the motion to proceed falling short of the 60-vote threshold in a 49–50 vote. The last-minute Sept. 14 rewrite included 126 Democratic-requested changes, covering state AG enforcement of ethics rules, a Treasury “circuit breaker” on stablecoin rewards if banks see deposit flight, and broader developer, miner, and validator safe harbors. The main sticking point was ethics language tied to official crypto holdings. The final text would have required covered officials and spouses to divest certain crypto interests or place them in a qualified blind trust, but critics argued it still left unresolved concerns around presidential crypto ventures.
